notes: Document stances: OTEAR agreed (delegates with three sample-statement tiers); OIT differed (A delegates, B restrict) and was resolved restrict because the page sets a university-wide fallback ('should not be considered permissible for coursework unless clearly stated or communicated by instructors'), as for the Newark OIT page. Main disagreements: (1) granularity: B split the chatbot-limits sentence, sample statement 2 and 3, the faculty-instructions sentence and the list of AI uses; both coders merged the bias/inaccuracy and copyright claims; resolved by splitting wherever a sentence held distinct rules (the copyright claim became a new P52 unit not found separately by either coder). (2) phase: sample statements (A course-start, B during-work) resolved during-work; confidential-data, fallback and OTEAR support sentences resolved as in Newark; faculty-guidance sentence resolved course-start; own-work quotation resolved general. (3) policy_type: integrity quotation (A P36, B P29) and code-of-conduct quotation resolved P29; test-your-assignments (A P35, B P63) resolved P63; project-with-explanation (A P34, B P35) and reflections (A P26, B P35) resolved P35; first-draft use P18 resolved P15 with a fit note; calculators sentence (B P45) resolved UNCOVERED. (4) actor/modality: fallback rule modality must-not resolved should-not (source says 'should not'); list of AI uses actor instructor/informs resolved all/may. (5) unit_stance: purchasing rule resolved neutral. Only-A units (1 OIT, 3 OTEAR) were all kept as real statements. Only-B units (12 OTEAR) were all kept, mostly finer splits plus a consultation offer and two cautions on output reliability. Matched counts aligned pairs; where B split an A unit, A's unit is paired with one of B's pieces and the others are counted only_B.
